title: Northern Laos in 9 Days: The Nam Ou River, Muang Ngoi, Hill-Tribe Villages and the Mekong
meta_title: Northern Laos 9 Days: Nam Ou River and Hill-Tribe Villages
meta_description: 9-day northern Laos journey: Nong Khiaw, a Nam Ou river cruise to Muang Ngoi and Muang Khua, Khmu and Hmong villages, treks and the Mekong at Pakbeng.
hero_alt: Limestone peaks over the Nam Ou river at Nong Khiaw
tagline: Slow boats, limestone peaks and villages few travellers reach
facts: Nong Khiaw 2, Muang Ngoi 1, Nam Kat Yorlapa (Oudomxay) 3, Pakbeng 1, Luang Prabang 1
Private car with driver, river boats, 4x4 and walking
intro: A small-group or private journey into Laos's mountainous north, for travellers who want village life and rivers rather than sights. From Luang Prabang you drive to Nong Khiaw under its limestone cliffs, cruise up the Nam Ou to car-free Muang Ngoi and on to Muang Khua, spend three nights at a nature resort in the Oudomxay forest with treks to Khmu, Hmong, Ikhor and Akha villages, then reach the Mekong at Pakbeng and return to Luang Prabang. Hydropower dams now cut the Nam Ou, so the boat trip includes a short change of boat at the dam. The tour starts with a morning departure from Luang Prabang, so arrive the day before; we suggest two extra nights there for the town itself.

best_time: November to February: dry, clear and cool (cold at dawn in the hills). March and April are hazy from field burning; May to October brings heavy rain and muddy trails.
seasons: Dry, sunny days and cool nights.
Smoke from field burning can hide the views.
Green and lush; muddy treks and high rivers.

faqs.q: How fit do we need to be?
faqs.a: Reasonably: treks are 1 to 4 hours on uneven, sometimes steep paths, and some boat landings need a scramble. Every trek can be shortened.

faqs.q: Can we add Luang Prabang sightseeing?
faqs.a: Yes. Two extra nights for the royal palace, Wat Xieng Thong, the Kuang Si waterfalls and the alms-giving.

faqs.q: Can this itinerary be changed for our dates and pace?
faqs.a: Yes. Every Blue Diamond Voyage itinerary is a starting point. We change the number of nights, the hotels, the pace and the activities to suit your family, and send you a personalised quote.

faqs.q: Do you look after vegetarian and Jain food?
faqs.a: Yes. We send your dietary brief to every hotel and guide before you travel, and suggest pure-vegetarian restaurants along the route. Jain meals without onion, garlic and root vegetables can be arranged in most places with notice.

faqs.q: Is there support while we travel?
faqs.a: Yes. You have our 24/7 travel desk on +91 97148 59797 and +91 98242 21400 and a WhatsApp group with your consultant for the whole trip.

good_to_know.title: Hotel deposit
good_to_know.text: Use a credit card for the deposit or pre-authorisation at check-in, never a forex or debit card. Forex cards cannot hold funds, many hotels refuse them, and a credit-card hold is released faster.

good_to_know.title: Kip and cash
good_to_know.text: Laos uses the kip. Cards work only in Luang Prabang hotels; carry kip and small US dollar notes for the north, where there are few ATMs.

good_to_know.title: Unexploded ordnance
good_to_know.text: Bombs from the 1960s and 70s still lie in rural Laos. Never leave marked paths or touch metal objects in the forest; stay with your guide.

good_to_know.title: Village etiquette
good_to_know.text: Ask before photographing people, do not enter homes or spirit houses without invitation, and give school supplies to the teacher rather than sweets to children.

good_to_know.title: Temples and trekking
good_to_know.text: Cover shoulders and knees in temples and remove shoes. Bring trekking shoes, a hat, insect repellent and a light rain jacket.

dining_intro: Lao food is rice, vegetables and herbs, so vegetarian meals are easy to arrange in Luang Prabang; in the north, our guide orders for you and the lodges cook to order.
dining_avoid: Fish sauce, padaek (fermented fish paste) and shrimp paste go into most dips and soups. Ask for 'bo sai nam pa' (no fish sauce).
food_card: Khoy kin jay. Bo kin sin, bo kin pa, bo kin khai. Bo sai nam pa, bo sai padaek. Khop jai.
We are strict vegetarians (Jain). No meat, fish, seafood or eggs. No onion, garlic, potato, carrot or any root vegetables. No meat or fish stock. Thank you.
